title: Sharp enough, but not too sharp
story: A receiver listens for a pilot tone at 1.59 kHz, made by a series 10 mH coil and 1 uF capacitor with the output across a resistor. The tone's transmitter drifts by up to 4 %, so 1.65 kHz must still come through within 6 dB. A strong interferer sits at 2 kHz and must be cut by at least 10 dB. The resistor sets the Q. Choose it.

goals.label: a drifted tone at 1.65 kHz still passes within 6 dB
the 2 kHz interferer is cut by at least 10 dB

hints: Q = sqrt(L / C) / R, and the bandwidth is f0 / Q. Here sqrt(L / C) = 100 ohm.
The pass band must be wide enough to include 1.65 kHz but narrow enough to cut 2 kHz.
